drafts.walkScript: Start with tree and leaf. A leaf is a small part of a tree. A petal is a small part of a flower. So petal fits. A garden and a vase can hold a flower, but neither is part of it.
Start with book and page. A page is one part inside a book. A room is one part inside a house. So room fits. A street and a neighbour are outside the house, not part of it.
Start with kitten and cat. A kitten is a young animal that grows into a cat. A puppy grows into a dog. So dog fits. A paw and whiskers are body parts, not the grown animal.
Start with sheep and lamb. A lamb is the baby of a sheep. A foal is the baby of a horse. So foal fits. A saddle goes on a horse, and a hoof is part of one.
Start with caterpillar and butterfly. A caterpillar grows into a butterfly. A tadpole grows into a frog. So frog fits. A tadpole has a tail, and a cocoon belongs to the butterfly story.
Start with leaf and tree. A leaf is a small part of a tree. A petal is a small part of a flower. So flower fits. A garden and a gardener are near flowers, but a petal is not part of them.
Start with seed and plant. A seed grows into a plant. An egg hatches into a chick. So chick fits. The shell is part of the egg, and a nest is where it sits.
Start with rabbit and burrow. A rabbit lives in a burrow. A bee lives in a hive. So hive fits. A sting is part of a bee, and honey is what it makes.
Start with spider and web. A spider builds a web as its home. A bird builds a nest as its home. So nest fits. Silk is what a web is made of, and a feather is part of a bird.
Start with car and road. A car travels along a road. A train travels along a track. So track fits. A carriage is part of a train, and a station is where it stops.
Start with captain and ship. A captain is in charge of a ship. A pilot is in charge of a plane. So plane fits. An anchor belongs to a ship, and a wing is only part of a plane.
Start with bee and honey. A bee makes honey. A cow makes milk. So milk fits. A horn is part of a cow, and grass is what it eats.
Start with foot and shoe. A shoe is worn on a foot. A hat is worn on a head. So hat fits. Hair grows on a head, and a head rests on a pillow, but neither is worn.
Start with hand and glove. A glove is worn on a hand. A sock is worn on a foot. So sock fits. A toe is part of a foot, and a foot stands on the floor.
Start with teacher and school. A teacher works in a school. A doctor works in a hospital. So hospital fits. A pupil belongs with the teacher, and medicine is what a doctor gives.
Start with day and sun. The sun shines in the sky by day. The moon shines in the sky at night. So moon fits. An owl comes out at night, and morning is part of the day.
Start with fish and swim. Swim is how a fish moves. Fly is how a bird moves. So fly fits. A bird can sing, but that is a sound, not how it moves. Float is not how a bird gets about.
Start with eye and see. An eye is used to see. An ear is used to hear. So hear fits. A whisper is a sound to hear, and look is what an eye does.
Start with pen and write. A pen is used to write. A knife is used to cut. So cut fits. Draw is another job for a pen. A knife can spread butter, but its main job is to cut.
Start with book and read. A book is something to read. A song is something to sing. So sing fits. Write goes with a book, and record is done to a song, not with your voice.
Start with winter and cold. Winter is a season that feels cold. Summer is a season that feels warm. So warm fits. Frosty belongs with winter, and long does not say how summer feels.
Start with whisper and quiet. A whisper is quiet. A shout is loud. So loud fits. Soft is like quiet, which suits a whisper. Angry is a feeling, not how a shout sounds.
Start with library and books. A library is a place that holds books. A gallery is a place that holds paintings. So paintings fits. A brush is used to paint, and a frame goes around a painting.

Start with chapter and novel. A chapter is one part of a novel. A scene is one part of a play. So play fits. A line is part of a scene, which turns the pair round. A ticket is only for watching a play.

Start with breeze and gale. A breeze is light wind and a gale is strong wind. A shower is light rain and a downpour is heavy rain. So downpour fits. Drizzle is lighter than a shower, the other way round. A kite goes with wind, not rain.

Start with novel and chapter. A chapter is one part of a novel. A verse is one part of a poem. So verse fits. A book is bigger than a poem, which turns the pair round. An author writes a poem but is not part of it.

Start with dictionary and word. A dictionary is a book full of words. An atlas is a book full of maps. So map fits. A library holds atlases, which turns the pair round. Geography is the subject, not what fills the book.

Start with sketch and painting. A sketch is a rough first try at a painting. A draft is a rough first try at an essay. So essay fits. An outline comes before a draft, which turns the pair round. A pen is only the tool.

Start with apprentice and master. An apprentice is a learner who grows into a master. A sapling is a young tree that grows into an oak. So oak fits. An acorn comes before a sapling, the other way round. A branch is only part of a tree.
